title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: Which statement correctly separates a workflow from an agent?

options.text: A workflow never calls a language model, while an agent always calls one
A workflow uses fewer tools than an agent does on every single request
In a workflow, code fixes the order of steps; in an agent, the model does
A workflow answers in one model call, while an agent needs at least two

items.stem: A makerspace assistant's program always runs these steps in this order: (1) ask the model to label the message as a manual question or a booking request; (2) if it is a manual question, search the manuals; if it is a booking request, check the calendar; (3) ask the model to write the reply from what was found. How should you classify this system?

options.text: An agent, because it calls the model more than once and uses tools
A workflow, because the code sets the steps and the model fills them in
An agent, because the model's label decides which branch the code takes
Neither, because a system with a language model cannot be a workflow

items.stem: Which part of the makerspace assistant is the strongest candidate for a fixed workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: Working out why a student's 3D print keeps failing, where each finding changes what to check next
Answering free-form questions that might need any one of several machine manuals
Planning a project across several machines when the needed steps are unknown at the start
Confirming a booking: check the calendar, check training, reserve the slot, send a receipt

items.stem: Your sponsor's model budget is small. In one sentence, give one reason a fixed workflow is usually cheaper and more predictable than an agent for a task whose steps are always the same.
In which situation does an agent earn its extra cost and unpredictability over a fixed workflow?

options.text: The steps needed cannot be known in advance, because each result changes what to do next
The task is identical every time, and the team wants the lowest possible cost per request
The team wants to avoid writing code that decides the order in which steps run
The task is high stakes, and the team wants the same steps followed every single time

items.stem: A teammate says, "Our booking flow calls a model at step 2, so it is an agent." In one sentence, what question would you ask to decide whether it is a workflow or an agent?
